newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Normandy sees rising gold reserves.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Normandy sees rising gold reserves.

text.p: Normandy Mining Ltd anticipates an increase in gold reserves, lower average cost of production, and an overall improvement at the KCGM Superpit, the company said in its annual report released on Thursday.

Managing director Tony Palmer said the company expected an increase in reserves as the Vera-Nancy (Queensland) and the Callie (Northern Territory) underground mines were developed and the extended basement feasability study at Boddington in Western Australia was completed.

A lower average cost of production was expected as the high grade Vera-Nancy and Callie mines commenced production, as well as an overall improvement at KCGM influenced in part by a more secure and lower cost power supply, he said in the report.
Vera-Nancy was expected to make an initial contribution to earnings in 1996/97 (to June 30), with production commencing early in calendar 1997, he said.
The future of the group's Bounty mine remains under a cloud, with Palmer saying its performance was the greatest disappointment in 1995/96 and was "under continuous scrutiny".
Normandy merged in August with Posgold Ltd and Gold Mines of Kalgoorlie Ltd and has launched a takeover bid for North Flinders Mines Ltd, in which it has a 72.5 percent stake.

"The company now has the financial strength and critical mass to enable an acceleration of its development as an internationally ranked and recognised gold miner," executive chairman Robert Champion de Crespigny said in the report.

In its corporate outlook for 1996/97, the report said the group would "achieve savings through rationalisation, complete North Flinders merger, review asset portfolio, (and) investigate North American listing."

Palmer said group exploration for 1996/97 consisted of Normandy-managed exploration of A$63 million, and A$32 million for projects managed by the group's La Source joint venture with the French BRGM group, with the allocation to gold related programmes increased to 83 percent of total budget.

Expenditure on the Goldfields gas and power line, Callie, Gossan Hill (Western Australia), and Boddington would continue in the current year at an aggregate budgeted cost of A$89.1 million, Palmer said.
Normandy's current group resources within Australia and New Zealand now stood at 26 million ounces of gold, with total reserves of 12.4 million ounces, the report said.
On a joint venture equity basis, the Mine Or share represented the addition of a further 4.5 million resource ounces and 2.2 million reserve ounces to the inventory.
